requirements.statement: Each link has a name (intitulé) given by its content, between its opening and closing tags.

citations.quote: Dans chaque page web, chaque lien a-t-il un intitulé entre `` et ``
Pour chaque lien, vérifier que le contenu de l’élément `<a>` (ou d’un élément pourvu d’un attribut WAI-ARIA `role=link`) contient un intitulé (texte ou alternative)
Balise possédant un attribut WAI-ARIA role="link" et dont l’action de navigation est prise en charge par un script.

routes.statement: The link contains text, in itself or in its child elements.

citations.quote: du texte contenu dans les éléments enfants du lien.

routes.statement: The link contains one or more images (img, role="img", object, canvas or svg) whose text alternative gives the name.

citations.quote: le « nom accessible » correspond au texte constitué à partir de l’alternative textuelle d’une ou plusieurs images dans le lien du type :

routes.statement: For an SVG link, a <title> element that is a direct child of the link, or the text of one or more <text> elements in it, gives the name.

citations.quote: Sinon, contenu de l’élément <title> enfant direct du lien ;
Sinon, contenu texte d’un ou plusieurs éléments <text>.
Balise <a> possédant un attribut xlink:href en SVG 1.1.

exceptions.statement: An <a> element used as an anchor, without href, is not a link and is not concerned.

citations.quote: Une ancre n’est pas un lien même si pendant longtemps l’élément `<a>` a servi de support à cette technique. Elle n’est donc pas concernée par le présent critère.

rationale.text: The wording asks for the name between and , and the methodology checks the content of the element for text or an alternative. So the routes are the forms of content the glossary lists: text, image alternatives, and for SVG links a child or <text> elements. Anchors without href are excluded by the technical note. axe's link-name is evidence only. It accepts aria-label, aria-labelledby and title, which are not content, so its clean result proves nothing. Its fault proves nothing for sure either: I could not confirm that its subtree text counts every image alternative the glossary counts (svg, object, canvas), and it skips role=link elements and SVG xlink:href links, so its scope is partial. The custom check computes the name from content only. Its fault is narrow: an <a> with href, rendered and exposed to assistive technologies, whose content gives no name, and which has no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title either. Such a link has no name at all, under the wording and under the glossary's note that a link without content fails 6.2, so the fault proves the test fails. A link whose only name is an attribute is cannot_tell: the wording rejects it, but I did not want a failure to rest on that reading alone. The entry is fail_only and not full, because one kind of element the test covers, an element with role=link, is a link only when a script handles its navigation, and code cannot decide that; the check abstains on such elements when their content gives no name. Applicability is judgment for the same reason. Needs is empty.

citations.quote: Note 4 : lorsqu’un lien ne comporte aucun contenu, il sera non conforme au regard du critère 10.2 et du critère 6.2.
Si c’est le cas pour chaque lien, **le test est validé**.
